newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat rises after EU grain auction.
newsitem.headline: French wheat rises after EU grain auction.

text.p: French wheat jumped further on Friday after the European Union granted more wheat than some exporters had expected at its weekly auction on Thursday, dealers said.
Meanwhile sellers stayed sidelined as frantic exporters looked for supplies to meet loading dealines in French ports.
Wheat into Rouen for March delivery was quoted at 895 francs per tonne, up five francs on Thursday and up 15 francs on the week.
April-May wheat into Rouen was paid at 880 francs per tonne against 875 francs on Thursday. All wheat prices exclude carrying charges.
"Sellers are now aiming for 900 francs per tonne, That's what is needed to secure substantial volumes," one dealer said.
On Thursday the EU granted 436,500 tonnes of soft wheat exports at a refund of 10.25 Ecus. The award, the biggest this season, will help absorb a licence squeeze.
MATIF fob barge wheat futures for May were bid at 928 francs per tonne and offered at 930 francs per tonne, but there was no trade.
